chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Self-respect, popular versus best music, and stories told in music
summary: Thompson says respect shows in music, the most profitable music is not always best, and the world has many stories to be told musically.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: As they say nowadays, do you know where I'm coming from, man? Do you know what that means, do you know where I'm coming from? That's what they say. Do you know where I'm coming from, when I'm telling you about that self respect?
Which all gets back to my music, because this comes out in your music. And I'm convinced that all these things that I'm talking about have to do with the music, you know?
And what may necessarily be the most popular music and the most profitable to the promoters and to the people who play it doesn't necessarily always have to be the best music.
And everybody can't be a Duke Ellington. You know.
But I think that there's a lot of music to be expressed in this world, a lot of stories to be told and to be heard, musically.
As I'm telling you now they should be heard.
There should be many, many stories.
